payload.query: Following the Parliamentary Research Service finding that education access declined significantly in 2023, what did MPs say in response and what remedies were proposed?

topk.text: about, we are still backsliding. The type of education we are doing is, to tell you the least, not relevant to our environment as a country. Hon Members — Dr Adutwum — rose — 79 6th December, 2023 80 Statements Mr Speaker: Hon Minister, do you still want to continue? Dr Adutwum: Mr Speaker, the Statement that I was responding to said: “Statement on the Decline of Quality Education”. That was the heading. I am not saying the decline happened here or did not. I am telling the House what we have done in order to attempt to arrest the decline. Mr Speaker, if I have your permission, I can speak to STEM education. I can speak to other interventions that have been done. Definitely, we are not where we need to be, but we are taking steps — Mr Speaker: Hon Minister, the Statement is not saying that nothing has been done to bring a change. First, let us admit there is a decline, then as we go through that, you can now bring in the interventions that will turn things around, but to start the way you did is like saying that what the Statement said is not true, and I beg to differ. Dr Adutwum — rose — Mr Speaker: Please, I said I would give you enough time to come back another day on this issue. I can see the Hon Member for Asawase. Yes, Hon Member? Alhaji Muntaka: Mr Speaker, I just want to draw the attention of my Hon Colleague, the Hon Minister for Education. Mr Speaker, you admitted a Statement under Orders 70, 71 or 72, and in commenting on those Statements, we, as a House are restricted to speaking to the limitations of the Statement. If he wants to make another Statement, he can come and do so, and we can contribute to his Statement with its own limitations, because Statements are not supposed to generate debate. Mr Speaker, the way the Minister is talking, you are right to say that it is like he is on the defence, and is saying that what the Statement has purported is inaccurate. This is exactly the problem we have, because we have reduced education in our country to scores or grades. It is either one scores A or 1. All of us in this Chamber who are at least 45 years and above know that it is not about scoring A or 1 that shows that one is well educated. It is about the product of the As and the 1s. When they come out, what do we see? That is what we are talking about. Mr Speaker, as an Hon Minister, he can come to make another Statement with its own limitations under Order 70, telling this House what he has done, then we can contribute to that one. For now, the Statement before us is what I gave him a

not work. Mr Speaker, when we come to senior high school (SHS), which Government is always touting as if nobody had ever enjoyed free SHS before, the conditions there are nothing to write home about. We would all agree that access has increased, but are we having quality education? We are not. Those who went to first year in December are going on holidays on Tuesday, and they are going to stay home for another three months. They will spend two months in school and then go and spend three months at home as holiday. In fact, they have disorganised the school calendar that even parents do not know when their wards will go to school. Government has said that more people are going to SHS, but it is on record that 194,862 candidates were not able to access secondary education between 2019 and 2023 because the infrastructure is not there to accommodate them. Mr Speaker, the President promised to build 350 new SHSs. As we speak today, he has not built even 10 per cent of that number. If he had continued with that vision of President John Dramani Mahama to construct 200 e-blocks, that would have given accommodation to 168,000 students. This deficit would have been reduced by more than 90 per cent. However, the Government has failed to do that. We are only talking about more people going to SHS, but we are silent over those who are unable to go. What crime have they committed? Mr Speaker, one other thing that is making education poor at the SHS level is the double-track system. The double- track system is affecting quality education as well. When we go to some of the schools, the dormitories are overcrowded as if the students are packed on one another. There is the fear that if nothing is done about that, we will not have a good environment for education. Government has not even told us when the double-track will end. There is no policy on sight to end the double- track system. So, it is important that as the President addressed the nation, he should have told us what steps they were taking to make sure that the double-track system comes to an end. Mr Speaker, the poor quality of food served in our SHSs should be our concern. Very soon, there will be a 97 29th February, 2024 98 Message on the State of the Nation, 2024 programme on Joy News, and we will see for ourselves the poor nature of the food that is being served to our students. Some parents have to go and even arrange with people to cook for their wards in the school. If one’s ward is in SHS now and they think that Government is feeding them, their child will come back home with kwashiorkor. That is the situation we find ourselves in. Mr Speaker, even the payment for supplies made to our schools is not coming. As we speak now, those who supplied school uniforms for two academic years have not been paid by Government.

have been referred to by some Hon Members in their submissions. It is not this Government. Nobody has said this Government is what is causing the decadence of education. No! They have traced it even to the time of the Provisional National Defence Council (PNDC), so do not be like you are on the defence. 77 6th December, 2023 78 Statements That is why I said that I am not sure you heard sufficiently to be able to respond. Can I give you an opportunity to come back with a Statement later on education because I am very much interested in this matter? Dr Adutwum: Mr Speaker, the Statement said that there is a decline in the quality, and Ghanaians are watching us. My Hon Colleague asked a question on the change in curriculum. The curriculum has been changed. So many different things are happening now. There has been a change in curriculum, and it is the implementation of that curriculum that is leading to the improvements that we are seeing in a number of schools across the country. Mr Speaker, the literacy rate of this country, which was at a point in time two per cent for primary two students in terms of proficiency, has risen to 38 per cent. We are not where we need to be — Mr Speaker: Proficiency in what? Dr Adutwum: Reading in primary two. Mr Speaker: Reading what? Dr Adutwum: Reading. Literacy. Mr Speaker: English or Twi? Dr Adutwum: English. Mr Speaker: Is that our language? It is one of the challenges they have pointed out. We do not develop any society using another society’s language. It is something we have to look at. Please, maybe, you will need to take the Official Report, go through it and come up with a comprehensive Statement, because we are the leaders. The political leaders are here. We are those who work on the manifestoes of the various political parties. If we see that there is a problem with our educational system, we have to lead and make sure that it changes. We will all agree in this country that corruption is systemic, and so the best way of solving corruption is to change the system. We are not prepared to change that system, but we keep on blaming each other. We are talking about education, and we know the problem. Nation building is a joint effort. We have formal and informal education. Most of the contributions are based on the formal. What about the informal sector? At our family and societal levels, what do we do to assist in education? Please, it is not about now or yesterday. Generally, we have seen that we have backslid. Even with the introduction of these new policies you are talking about, we are still backsliding. The type of education we are doing is, to tell you the least, not relevant to our environment as a country. Please, I think I would give you another opportunity to come with a Statement on this matter, so that we look at it again.

Apaak, the facts are subjective. I am not aware. You may be aware, but somebody else may not be aware of that. Just withdraw that part for me. Hear!] Again, in the area of education, for the first time in the history of our Republic, our sons, daughters, brothers and sisters who have disabilities are enjoying free education at the tertiary level. That was not enough for His Excellency the President. His Excellency the President working with the Minister for Education, is introducing another intervention that would provide free education for learners with disabilities from the very basic level to the senior high school level, then when they transition to the university, they get free education. So, essentially, H.E. John Dramani Mahama is introducing a policy that would make education from kindergarten to university free for all persons with disability. [Hear! Hear!] Mr Second Deputy Speaker: Be winding up please, your time is almost up. Dr Apaak: For eight years, they spent our money excavating the biggest hole on the surface of the universe. They had no foresight. They spent our hard- earned resources chartering luxurious flights so that they can freshen up in the air to the detriment of Ghanaians. So, let no one make a mistake that H.E. John Dramani Mahama and the NDC Government— Mr Second Deputy Speaker: Hon Members, we turn to Mr Matthew Nyindam. [Hear! Hear!] Mr Matthew Nyindam (NPP — Kpandai): Thank you Hon—[Uproar] Mr Second Deputy Speaker: Mr Dafeamkpor, the Majority have had five commentaries, the Minority, four. We are now going to the fifth. 4:21 p.m. Mr Dafeamekpor: Mr Speaker, I am making this intervention on Constitutional grounds. Yesterday, 24th November, 2025, the High Court of Tamale ordered that the outcome of the election—these are very serious matters, that the outcome of the 7th December elections 2024, which brought the Hon Matthew Nyindam to this House, as MP for Kpandai was flawed, and therefore that election has been ordered to be rerun. Mr Speaker, ipso facto, Hon Matthew Nyindam is no longer a Member of this House. He is not. Hear me, so that he can respond. So, by 97 26th November, 2025 98 Government’s Financial Policy, 2026 operation of law, he is no longer a Member of this House with a voice. That is one. Mr Speaker, two, we have received the court orders and received proof of service. The orders of the court have been duly served on Parliament. It was served yesterday. It will serve the Minority to listen to me in silence. If they are minded to respond, then they can do so. Mr Second Deputy Speaker: Hon Members, please, let us listen to him. Mr Dafeamekpor: Mr Speaker, I have a copy of the proof of service of the orders of the Tamale High Court, dated, 24th November, 2025 and served to Parliament. The orders of the court were served by the court bailiff of the High Court, Accra.

the Hon Minister for Education have vamoosed and are no longer captured. How can that be possible at a time like this with all the challenges we have in the educational sector? So, I am pleading with Leadership to reconsider because some of the matters are urgent and time- sensitive. I do not know the justification as to why the Questions have been admitted and advertised for the past two weeks, but in the Business Statement for the ensuing week, they have suddenly disappeared. Please, I am on my knees. This country's educational system is on the verge of a crisis and we need to rescue it— My fellow Vandal says I should kneel down. He knows what we do in Commonwealth Hall. I so submit. Mr Peter Lanchene Toobu: Thank you, Mr Speaker, for the opportunity. Let me thank Leadership for the good job done. I realised that the Hon Minister for the Interior is slated to be in the House next week to answer about six Questions. Mr Speaker, something is happening in the 53 12th July, 2024 54 Business of the House country and everybody is getting worried. There is a sound of recruitment in the air. If we go to the National Police Training School (NPTS), currently as I speak to you, there are young men and women who are there hoping to go through medical examinations, and this is the first time I have heard that the recruitment process starts with medical examination. It has never happened in history. Mr Speaker, I filed an Urgent Question, and I am surprised to look through this document and not find it. I would want clarity on whether it was not admitted or it was admitted but was found not suitable to be answered. Probably, if you can do that during the Committee of the Whole, I would appreciate it. The people of Ghana are waiting to hear something from the Hon Minister for the Interior regarding the current recruitment stories all over the media space. Mr Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa: Thank you very much, Mr Speaker. Mr Speaker, you would recall that last week after the presentation of the Business Statement, I submitted that I had taken intelligence that the Volta River Authority (VRA) would soon spill excess water from the Akosombo Dam. Later that day, in the evening, the VRA put out a statement confirming that they were about to spill excess water. Indeed, they have begun stakeholder consultations in our communities to prepare the minds of those of us who live near the dam to get ready for another spillage. Mr Speaker, it is with a heavy heart that I remind you and this House that it has been 10 good months since the September 15th spillage, which unleashed untold disaster and devastation. More than 60,000 people were displaced. In my constituency, there were more than 12,000 people that were displaced. Ten months ago, we filed a Motion, and the Speaker assured us that there would be a Committee of enquiry so that, most importantly, we learn lessons.

MPs acknowledged that education access declined significantly and agreed with the Parliamentary Research Service's finding [2fc50d4e2a88b6bf595eef06a7e0ea916fc876c9f0060a7868a860ee4fe7bf99:42]. They proposed remedies such as improving infrastructure, increasing funding for education, and implementing policies to address the decline in quality education [a746e898a2ed99dc09e7ce2df6545ff61f7318d86d5018df35d84dbb5e8ca61f:52]. Additionally, MPs suggested that the government should focus on providing free education for learners with disabilities from kindergarten to university level [c3550d590f1c02ab826a61b42b1d6edd4304390ef5191d6da111396f6ee04ddf:50].

Note: I don't have enough evidence in the retrieved documents to answer questions about what MPs said in response and what remedies were proposed.
